claims: President Donald Trump fired Pam Bondi as U.S. Attorney General on April 2, 2026.
Pam Bondi's tenure as U.S. Attorney General was 14 months.
Reports indicate the firing of Pam Bondi was driven by President Donald Trump's frustration over her handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files.
Reports indicate the firing of Pam Bondi was driven by a lack of successful prosecutions against President Donald Trump's political opponents.
President Donald Trump replaced Pam Bondi with Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche.
Sources cited dissatisfaction with Pam Bondi's performance.
Sources cited dissatisfaction with Pam Bondi's handling of the Epstein case.
Pam Bondi was scheduled to testify about the Epstein case before the House Oversight Committee.
Pam Bondi's 14-month term was one of the shortest for a confirmed Attorney General.
Pam Bondi's term ended amidst pressure from within the administration.
The pressure included pressure from outside advisor Bill Pulte.
President Donald Trump officially stated Pam Bondi was "transitioning to a much needed and important new job in the private sector".
Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche was named as Pam Bondi's replacement.
